To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

microtubules treated with the antimitotic drug taxol can be disassembled and reassembled reversibly by shifting the temperature in the presence millimolar levels Ca2+ and that taxol dissociates from microtubule subunits during disassembly.
reversible disassembly of taxol-treated tubulin can be achieved by a combination of Ca2+ and temperature and that the taxol is dissociated from the tubulin during disassembly.

microtubules that are stabilized with taxol can be induced to depolymerize and reassemble in cycles, that the binding of taxon to tubulin can therefore be reversed, and that MAPs can be recovered by this procedure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reversible disassembly of taxol-treated polymer and with the reassembly of tubulin from the disassembled state.
the reversible assembly of taxotreated microtubules and with the role that microtubuleassociated proteins play in this process.
the assembly of microtubule proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
taxol can be removed from microtubules and that the microtubules so treated are competent to assemble and disassemble in a reversible fashion.
the binding of taxon to tubulin is reversible, but that it is a slow process.
taxol is a very potent stabilizer of microtubule polymers, but the binding is reversible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
reversible cycles of microtubule assembly/disassembly can be achieved with taxol-stabilized microtubule proteins.
taxol is a reversible stabilizing agent for microtubule assembly.
taxol-treated tubulin is competent to reassemble under conditions that depolymerize untreated microtubule proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
taxol can be removed from microtubules, and this is important in terms of how we understand the mechanism of action of taxol and how we purify and work with microtubules in general.
microtubule proteins can be reversibly assembled and disassembled, and that taxol is not required to stabilize the assembly.
microtubule assembly is not an irreversible process.
